short: The only native ruler recognised as Prince of Wales, and the last of them.
full:
Llywelyn ap Gruffudd took sole control of Gwynedd after defeating his brothers at Bryn Derwin in 1255, then expanded east and south while England was distracted by the barons' war. He adopted the title Prince of Wales in 1258, and by the Treaty of Montgomery in 1267 Henry III recognised it, along with the homage of the other Welsh lords, in exchange for a heavy annual payment Llywelyn could not sustain.

Edward I was less accommodating. Llywelyn's refusal to do homage in person brought invasion in 1277 and a settlement that stripped him of everything east of the Conwy. When his brother Dafydd began a fresh rising in 1282 Llywelyn joined it, and was killed near Builth that December in a skirmish away from his main army; his head was displayed in London. The Statute of Rhuddlan annexed the principality to the English crown in 1284.
